After officers extracted Tatiana and Michael, both received medical care and were transported from the scene. Tatiana died from her injuries. Both forensic and autopsy reports indicate she was struck solely by Michael's gunfire, not by officers. Despite multiple gunshot wounds, Michael survived after being airlifted for treatment. He was later charged with one count of abduction, one count of murder, 12 counts of use of firearm in commission of a felony, nine counts of attempted aggravated murder of a law enforcement officer, one count of shooting a missile at a law enforcement vehicle, one count of discharging a weapon from a vehicle, one count of a looting and one count of possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. Apparently while in jail, he also caught one count of malicious wounding by mob. Michael pleaded not guilty to all charges, leading to a jury trial. During testimony, he claimed he fired only after officers shot at him first, a version of events that appears to conflict with the footage. After just 65 minutes of deliberation, the jury found Michael guilty on, one count of abduction, one count of murder, 10 counts of use of firearm and commission of a felony, Three counts of attempted aggravated murder of a law enforcement officer and one count of eluding a police officer. All other charges were dismissed. Although he was convicted in March 26, he has not yet been sentenced at the time of this publication. Court records list a pre-sentence report hearing for September 25, 26. A go-fund me supporting Tatiana's four-year-old son remains active. The fundraiser is organized by her brother, who first reported the abduction. A link is available in the description below.
